title: A rational map agreeing with a morphism along a smooth section extends near that section
statement: Let $B,T,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T$ normal Noetherian: it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings, and every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $t:T\to B$ and $r:Y\to B$ be morphisms, with $r$ separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]). Let $q:X\to T$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with a section $a:T\to X$, so $q\circ a=\operatorname{id}_T$; regard $X$ as a $B$-scheme by $t\circ q$. Let $D\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme, let $v:D\to Y$ be a $B$-morphism, and let $b:T\to Y$ be a $B$-morphism. Put $T^\circ=a^{-1}(D)$. Suppose $T^\circ$ contains every $z\in T$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{T,z}\leq1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $v\circ a|_{T^\circ}=b|_{T^\circ}$. Then there is an open subscheme $N\subseteq X$ containing $a(T)$ and a $B$-morphism $\widetilde v:N\to Y$ whose restriction to $N\cap D$ is $v|_{N\cap D}$. No group structure on $Y$, quasi-compactness of $X$ or $Y$, or separatedness of $q$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED. Extracted section form of the argument (replace the first projection and diagonal by a smooth morphism and its section, and the unit section by b); not a quotation of the theorem statement.

proof.text: The source $X$ is normal by [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], and reduced and locally Noetherian by [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback], since $T$ has those properties. Let $V$ be the union of all open subsets $L\subseteq X$ admitting a $B$-morphism $v_L:L\to Y$ agreeing with $v$ on $L\cap D$. On overlaps these morphisms agree by [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext]: the overlap is reduced, its intersection with the dense open $D$ is dense, and both structural composites to $B$ are $tq$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to a $B$-morphism $v_V:V\to Y$, and $D\subseteq V$.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $T_V=a^{-1}(V)$. The two $B$-morphisms $v_Va$ and $b$ on $T_V$ agree on $T^\circ$. This open is dense in $T$ because it contains every generic point, whose local ring has dimension zero; thus it is dense in $T_V$. Since $T$ is reduced, [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] gives $v_Va=b$ on $T_V$. It remains to show $a(T)\subseteq V$.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $z\in T$ and put $x=a(z)$. Choose an affine open $B_0\subseteq B$ containing $t(z)$ and an affine open $H\subseteq r^{-1}(B_0)$ containing $b(z)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; the maps to these opens factor by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Choose an affine neighbourhood $W_0$ of $x$ in $(tq)^{-1}(B_0)$. It is Noetherian: it is locally Noetherian by step 1 and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its topology is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Its normal integral components are open and closed by [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components]. Retain the component containing $x$ and then an affine neighbourhood $W_1$ of $x$ inside that component. This $W_1$ is normal integral Noetherian by the same local Noetherian and affine quasi-compact argument.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Set $T'=a^{-1}(W_1)\cap b^{-1}(H)\cap t^{-1}(B_0)$ and $W=W_1\cap q^{-1}(T')$. These are open neighbourhoods of $z,x$. The restricted section $a':T'\to W$ has retraction $q':W\to T'$; $q'$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Both schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Their normality and the integrality of $W$ follow by restricting local rings and nonempty opens. Put $J=W\cap V\cap v_V^{-1}(H)$ and factor $v_V|_J$ through $H$ using [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. The dense open $T'\cap T^\circ$ is nonempty, and its section lies in $J$ by step 2 and $b(T')\subseteq H$. Hence $J$ is a nonempty open of integral $W$, so is dense.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-affine-rational-indeterminacy] to $J\to H$ on $W$. Obtain its maximal extension $h_E:E\to H$ and closed boundary $F=W\setminus E$ of pure codimension one, or empty. The composite $E\to H\to Y$ is a $B_0$-morphism: its structural map to $B_0$ agrees with $tq$ on dense $J$, hence on reduced $E$ by [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext]. Here the affine $B_0$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: on affine charts its diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication map $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\to R$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$. On $E\cap V$, the maps $h_E$ (composed to $Y$) and $v_V$ therefore agree by that same relative equality lemma, since they agree on dense $J\cap E\cap V$. In particular $h_E$ agrees with $v$ on $E\cap D$, so $E\subseteq V$.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely $a'^{-1}(E)=a'^{-1}(V)$. Only the inclusion from right to left needs proof. For $w\in T'$ with $a'(w)\in V$, step 2 gives $v_V(a'(w))=b(w)\in H$, so $a'(w)\in J\subseteq E$. Thus $a'^{-1}(F)=T'\setminus a'^{-1}(V)$. This set contains no point $w$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{T',w}\leq1$: the open immersion $T'\subseteq T$ preserves its local ring, and all such points lie in $T^\circ\subseteq a^{-1}(V)$ by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-divisor-intersection] to $q',a',F$. It forces $a'^{-1}(F)=\varnothing$. In particular $x=a'(z)\in E\subseteq V$.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every $z\in T$ was arbitrary, so $a(T)\subseteq V$. Take $N=V$ and $\widetilde v=v_V$ from step 1. The construction already gives its $B$-linearity and the stated restriction to $N\cap D$. All neighbourhoods were local; no finite cover of $X$ or $Y$ was taken. If $T$ is empty then $X$ is empty (because $q$ exists) and the unique map on $N=\varnothing$ suffices.

source.place: BLR §4.4, Lemma 2 and proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116); primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.
